definitions.explanation: Characteristic of or appropriate for a young child; lacking sophistication or maturity.
Relating to the stage of early childhood development (neutral usage).

examples.japanese: そんな{幼稚|ようち}な{言|い}い{訳|わけ}は{通|とお}らない。
examples.english: Such a childish excuse won't work.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{考|かんが}え{方|かた}は{幼稚|ようち}だ。
examples.english: His way of thinking is immature.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{幼稚|ようち}園で{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing at kindergarten.
examples.notes: Neutral usage in {幼稚|ようち}{園|えん} (kindergarten)

notes:
USAGE: {幼稚|ようち} has two main contexts:
1. Negative: describing immature or childish behavior in adults (pejorative)
2. Neutral: relating to early childhood education

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{幼稚|ようち}な{考|かんが}え (childish thinking)
・{幼稚|ようち}な{行動|こうどう} (immature behavior)

COMPOUND:
・{幼稚|ようち}{園|えん} (kindergarten) - very common word using neutral sense

RELATED:
・{子供|こども}っぽい - childish (more colloquial)
・{未熟|みじゅく} - immature, inexperienced
・{大人|おとな}げない - unbecoming of an adult
